attacks.claim: Dark-mode regression: `.day-card` hardcodes `background: #ffffff` instead of `var(--surface)`, so under prefers-color-scheme: dark (about 30% of users) light-gray text (#f2f2f7) sits on a white card, making tile titles and metadata near-unreadable. QA was light-mode only, so this would ship unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } inside a dark-mode-aware stylesheet where --text becomes #f2f2f7; QA: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"

attacks.claim: Dark-mode muted metadata (#a1a1a6) on the hardcoded #ffffff card has roughly 2.4:1 contrast, below WCAG AA. No dark-mode contrast check exists in the QA report.
attacks.evidence: .tile .meta { color: var(--muted); } with --muted: #a1a1a6 in dark mode over .day-card { background: #ffffff; }; ABSENT: any dark-mode contrast check in the QA report

attacks.claim: The fixed 72px mobile action bar has no bottom padding or spacer on `.planner`, so the Sunday card and the bottom of its tile list can be hidden behind the bar when scrolled to the end. The bar also ignores the iOS safe-area inset.
attacks.evidence: "Sunday is the last child of .planner" and .action-bar { position: fixed; height: 72px; } with .planner { padding: 16px; } and no bottom offset; ABSENT: padding-bottom or spacer for the fixed bar

attacks.claim: Tile images are 320px intrinsic width with no responsive constraint. On 360px phones (about 296px usable inside padding) the image overflows the card horizontally.
attacks.evidence: with no img rule such as max-width: 100% in planner.css

attacks.claim: The most frequent action (adding a recipe's ingredients to the list, about 9.4/week, 64% on mobile) goes from one tap to a multi-step path, and the one-tap '+ List' button is removed. This regresses the core workflow for 100% of users, and the artifact does not show it was validated against this usage.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level '+ List' button is removed to declutter tiles." and "tap the tile → recipe page → 'Ingredients' tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → 'Add to list' → toast with 'Undo'."

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' adds up to 21 recipes in one action with no stated behavior for partial failure, retries, double-tap idempotency, duplicate handling, or confirmation. A mid-batch failure could leave the list half-populated, and repeated taps could duplicate entries.
attacks.evidence: "'Generate shopping list' (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; ABSENT: failure, retry, or duplicate-handling behavior

attacks.claim: The rollback claim is asserted, not shown. The flag restores the old UI only if the old planner can read data written by the new drag-between-days move and bulk shopping-list action. The artifact does not say those writes use the existing schema.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"; ABSENT: schema compatibility for the new move and bulk-add writes

attacks.claim: Ships to 100% of web users at once for a core-interaction change, with no ramp or canary. The watch list has no thresholds, owners, or alert conditions, so there is no defined trigger for flipping the flag off.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind planner_v7" and "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode and two light-mode viewports. It does not cover the 360px width, the dark-mode path, or the sticky bar overlap, yet the report claims pass.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%."

attacks.claim: Drag-to-move is the primary move interaction on a touch-first mobile audience, but touch drag behavior is not described and the drag QA does not name a touch device. Drag may conflict with scrolling.
attacks.evidence: "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it." and "Drag-and-drop between days, 'Move to…' menu ... : pass." (no touch device named)

attacks.claim: The undo toast has no stated live-region announcement or timeout duration, so screen-reader users may miss the confirmation or lose Undo before using it.
attacks.evidence: "→ 'Add to list' → toast with 'Undo'."; ABSENT: aria-live or timeout length

attacks.claim: Terminology is inconsistent across the flow ('+ List', 'Add to list', 'Generate shopping list'), which may confuse users about whether these are the same action.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level '+ List' button" vs "'Add to list'" vs "'Generate shopping list'"
